clue.text: Might train crash? Assuredly!

parts.note: might, as in strength or power, means force

indicators.note: a crash wrecks the train, so its letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a train could crash and is told that it certainly might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb asking a question, but it is a noun meaning strength; 'crash' rearranges the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean without any doubt; an adverb phrase of certainty.

clue.text: Brave front

explanation.surface: A bold face put on things.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave a danger is to confront it head-on, and a building's facade or front is also so named.

clue.text: Fish seen in the round staggering

indicators.note: the fish is seen inside the round, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a ring is a round shape
an eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A fish turns up in a ring, lurching about unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' could suggest an amazing catch, but it is the definition meaning tottering.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe swaying and lurching unsteadily on one's feet.

clue.text: Exile unruly pixie to a tarn

indicators.note: unruly suggests disorder, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly behaved sprite is banished to a mountain lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' shuffles PIXIE TO A TARN; a tarn is a small mountain lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is banishment from one's homeland, the same as being sent abroad for good.

clue.text: Face the bowling and assume control

explanation.surface: A batsman goes in to bat and takes charge of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end; a batsman facing it takes the over.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman receives a bowler's set of six deliveries, and a new boss gains command of a firm.

clue.text: Complete, in opening of the performance

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from the word the

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: An actor reports that a show went entirely to plan from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged is complete.

clue.text: Kit's pointless joke

indicators.note: a compass point is removed, here E for East

parts.note: to kit out is to equip

explanation.surface: Someone called Kit cracks a joke that has no point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes E, a compass point, from EQUIP; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip is a witty remark or wisecrack.

clue.text: To increase subsidy to British Rail causes reproach

parts.note: to up a price is to increase it
BR is the abbreviation for British Rail, the former UK national railway
aid is financial help or a subsidy

explanation.surface: Raising the grant to the national railway draws public criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail was the state-owned UK railway until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or censure someone severely is to reproach them.

clue.text: Can't pet, for a change, get liquorice here?

indicators.note: for a change means the letters are altered into a different order

explanation.surface: Unable to stroke an animal, someone wonders if they can buy sweets here instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change' rearranges CANT PET FOR. Pontefract, a Yorkshire town, is famous for liquorice and its Pontefract cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshire town long known for growing liquorice and making liquorice sweets.

clue.text: Skinflint's fish-market bargain

parts.note: something cheap is a bargain
a skate is a flat fish sold at market

explanation.surface: A miser's idea of a good buy is a cut-price fish at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser or stingy person who avoids spending money.

clue.text: Port gets round prohibition

parts.note: O is round in shape
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A harbour town finds a way to get around a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish harbour town on the west coast.

clue.text: Medium may have it concealed in a lacy cover

indicators.note: concealed means disguised, so these letters are disguised by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller hides something under a lace cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' looks like a hiding signal, but nothing is hidden; it rearranges IN A LACY COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist medium is supposed to have second sight, the power to see beyond normal perception.

clue.text: Record deviation from the vertical

explanation.surface: Notes on how far a building leans.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is a written record of items, and a ship leaning to one side has a tilt.

clue.text: I left! various localities to go to and fro

indicators.note: various suggests varied arrangements, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has moved through many places swings back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' says I is removed from the mixed letters of LOCALITIES; what is left of the jumble is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To swing back and forth like a pendulum.

clue.text: Take exception to dancing on the billiard table

parts.note: to object is to take exception
a ball is an occasion for dancing

explanation.surface: Someone protests at people dancing on top of a snooker table.
explanation.walkthrough: On a billiard table it is the ball struck by the cue ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards or snooker, the ball the cue ball is aimed at.

clue.text: Responsible for the issue of Scottish notes

definitions.text: Responsible for the issue of Scottish notes

parts.words: Responsible for the issue of Scottish notes
parts.note: the surface suggests a Scottish bank printing banknotes; the musical notes come from a Highland instrument

explanation.surface: Who prints the banknotes in Scotland?
explanation.walkthrough: Scottish banks issue their own banknotes, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland wind instrument that produces musical notes.

clue.text: Songs the Fuhrer heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken out loud, giving its sound not spelling

parts.note: Führer is German for leader

explanation.surface: Hitler is overheard singing German songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert.
explanation.definitionFit: German art songs for voice and piano.

clue.text: Graphite the origin of possible back-trouble?

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, taken here from possible

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A pencil lead might be to blame for an aching back.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the mineral graphite, used in pencils.

clue.text: Personality I'd left in being

indicators.note: left means gone away, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: identity is a person's individual character
the contraction I'd written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone's character has been left behind in a living thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes ID from IDENTITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing with independent existence is a being.

clue.text: Poor Ted! Blown up by a missile!

indicators.note: something blown up is shattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Ted is blown up by a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' rearranges POOR TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater weapon fired at ships.

clue.text: East European star returns in one piece (almost)

indicators.note: in means one word goes inside the other
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a slice is one piece of a cake or loaf

indicators.note: returns means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nova is a star that flares suddenly

explanation.surface: An East European film star comes back from abroad all in one piece, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns NOVA into AVON, which goes 'in' SLIC (SLICE with 'almost' removing the E).
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Slavs of eastern Europe and their languages.

clue.text: Worn out, I put into German city

indicators.note: worn out suggests something knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ich is the German word for I

explanation.surface: Exhausted, someone moves to a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WORN into NORW; 'German city' misleads, as German only translates I. Norwich is a city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is an English cathedral city in Norfolk.

clue.text: One quarter in true, in direct descent

indicators.note: in means these letters are put inside the word for true

parts.note: leal is an old Scots word for loyal or true
I is the Roman numeral for one
N is a compass quarter, north

explanation.surface: A family tree shows a quarter of the line running straight down.
explanation.walkthrough: N for north is one of the four quarters of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Descended in an unbroken line from parent to child.

clue.text: Intimidation from teacher or backing during school-days

indicators.note: during means these letters come inside the school period

parts.note: a term is a period of school days

indicators.note: backing means the words are read in reverse

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A child is bullied either by a teacher or by friends of one during term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SIR OR into RORIS, which goes 'during' TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Using violence and fear to coerce people.

clue.text: Historic city in Surrey or Kent?

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A quiz asks whether a famous city lies in one of two southern English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey and Kent are counties of south-east England; the city is in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient walled city in northern England.

clue.text: A type of fish or sca-weed

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Something found in the sea is either a fish or a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly extracted from red algae, used for culturing microbes.

clue.text: One who 'as to declare

indicators.note: the dropped H in 'as signals that the initial H is lost from the word

parts.note: one who has something is a haver

explanation.surface: A Cockney who owns something must state it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as is has with a Cockney dropped H, so the one who has is HAVER without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To state firmly or assert something.

clue.text: Commonly salesman is out to get initial and follow-up decoration

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative
said commonly, is not in becomes ain't in

indicators.note: initial means the first letter, here of get

explanation.surface: A salesman is away, trying to find the start and end of a decorating job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks the slang ain't: 'is out' is 'is not in', commonly AIN'T IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a fresh coat after the earlier one, so a second decorating job.

clue.text: The machine to appear indistinctly

explanation.surface: A machine looms up out of the fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A loom is a weaving frame, and to loom is to emerge vaguely and threateningly.

clue.text: Singer — baffle her completely

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
to get someone is to puzzle or baffle them, as in 'that gets me'

explanation.surface: A singer completely confuses a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means entirely, wholly.
